title: Jackfruit Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Jackfruit Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Jackfruit nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in langka, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Jackfruit nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your langka (jackfruit) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, boron, zinc, magnesium and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Nitrogen deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for jackfruit
heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, zinc and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which jackfruit nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Jackfruit nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of langka
rows: old, lower leaves, the whole plant

old, lower leaves, leaf edges and tips

Muriate of potash 0 0 60, Sulfate of potash 0 0 50
A slow, stunted tree whose older leaves turn dull with a purple or bronze tint underneath.
old, lower leaves, between the veins
Older leaves yellow between the side veins, from the edge in toward the midrib, while the veins stay green.

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of langka

Fruits split or crack with a reddish purple color and gum in the cracks. Young leaves yellow and brittle.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a jackfruit nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest jackfruit nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in jackfruit

Jackfruit shows it like most fruit trees. The tree first looks light green all over. Then the older, lower leaves turn evenly yellow, veins included, and fall early, while the yellowing slowly moves up to younger leaves. New flushes are short with small leaves, and the tree sets fewer fruits. You see it most at this stage: young trees in the first years after planting, and old bearing trees that never get fertilizer.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in langka

In the Philippines jackfruit is seldom fertilized, so many trees run short. Sandy or eroded soils low in organic matter, heavy rain that washes nitrogen away. Weeds or grass competing under the canopy make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on old leaves, but the yellow sits between the veins while the veins stay green. Jackfruit does not tolerate wet soil, and two or three days of standing water can yellow and kill a tree. To be sure, send a sample of recently matured leaves for a leaf test and a soil sample for a soil test. A clear greening of new leaves within a few weeks after a nitrogen dose confirms it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

For young trees, the Philippine practice described by Coronel gives 100 to 150 grams of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per tree one month after planting and the same again six months later. Fruiting trees take 0.5 to 1 kg of Complete 14 14 14 each when the rains begin and the same amount again as they end. At least 2 to 3 kg per dose for full grown trees of 15 to 20 years. Spread it in a ring under the canopy edge and water it in.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Ammonium Chloride** by La Filipina (25 0 0), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year in two splits, raise the amount as the tree grows. Keep a mulch or compost ring under the canopy. Let a soil test and the crop's color set the season's nitrogen.
Potassium deficiency in jackfruit

The signs on jackfruit are those of most fruit trees. The edges and tips of older or newly matured leaves yellow first, then dry brown as a scorch that moves in toward the midrib. Badly hit leaves drop. Fruit and seed production suffers, so fruits are smaller and lower in quality. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, most of all during fruit growth when the fruit pulls potash from the leaves.
Why potassium deficiency happens in langka
Heavy crops remove potash every year, and most trees get none back. Sandy, leached soils under heavy rain and dry spells that cut uptake make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also hits old leaves but yellows between the veins, not along the edge. Fertilizer burn from too much fertilizer close to the trunk and dry wind can also brown leaf edges. To be sure, A leaf test of recently matured leaves and a soil test for exchangeable potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Give potash with the yearly fertilizer, following the soil test. Feed each EVIARC Sweet tree 0.83 kg Complete 14 14 14, 3.33 kg Solophos and 0.73 kg Muriate of potash 0 0 60. Fed trees bear bigger pulp and more flakes per fruit than unfed ones. The usual schedule rises from 0.1 kg potash per tree in the first year to 0.5 kg from the sixth year, in two splits.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash every year, split in two doses, and return leaves and fruit waste to the ring as compost.
Phosphorus deficiency in jackfruit

Jackfruit shows it the way most fruit trees do. Growth is slow and the tree stays small. Older leaves lose their shine and take on a purple or bronze color, most of all on the underside. Roots stay weak and young trees take longer to start bearing. You see it most at this stage: young trees after planting, and trees on very acid soils.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in langka
Acid soils that lock phosphorus up, soils low in organic matter, and cold or waterlogged soil.
How to tell it apart

Cool weather, drought and root damage can also slow growth and redden leaves, so check the soil moisture and the roots. Nitrogen deficiency makes old leaves pale yellow rather than purple or bronze. To be sure, A soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer in a ring under the canopy and work it into the topsoil, following the soil test. Give 3.33 kg Solophos (Superphosphate 0 20 0) per tree, along with complete fertilizer and potash. The usual schedule gives 0.08 kg phosphorus per tree in the first year, rising to 0.4 kg from the sixth year. Lime very acid soils so the phosphorus stays available. Give it when the rains begin.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mix compost and a phosphorus fertilizer into the planting soil, and add some every year.
Boron deficiency in jackfruit

Fruits split or crack, and the cracks show a reddish purple color with gum oozing out. Young leaves turn yellow, thin and brittle, and the shoot tips grow poorly. Flowers can drop before they are pollinated, which leaves misshapen fruit. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit growth, and on new flushes.
Why boron deficiency happens in langka
Sandy or leached soils low in organic matter, dry spells, and heavy liming. Boron moves little inside the tree, so young tissue and fruit show it first.
How to tell it apart

Rhizopus fruit rot makes young fruits go soft and grey black with mould, not dry cracks with gum. Fruit borers leave holes with frass. To be sure, do a soil test, and a leaf test for boron. Cracked fruit together with yellow, brittle young leaves points to boron. In a soil test, less than 0.5 ppm of boron is low.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Spread about 10 kg of Borax per hectare on the soil, or spray it on the leaves at 1 gram per liter (16 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Do not mix boron with calcium fertilizers or apply it together with ammonium fertilizers. Too much boron is toxic, so do not repeat high doses without a test. Give boron before flowering: flowers and fruit set need it most.

Sold here with boron: **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl Chem (11 percent boron), **Fertibagra 15G** by Unilox Far East Resources (14.6 percent boron), **B17 (Boric Acid)** by Newman Chemicals (17 percent boron) and **Better Yield** by Bacphil Planters Fertilizer (0 0 0.9 with 10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up, water during long dry spells, and add a small boron dose on soils that tested low. Test the soil every two or three years.
Zinc deficiency in jackfruit

New leaves come out small with short stalks and crowd together at the shoot tip in a rosette. They yellow between the veins and can show yellow streaks. Fruits stay smaller and more of them drop, so the yield falls. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, flowering and early fruit growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in langka
Zinc is the most common micronutrient shortage of fruit crops. Soils with pH outside about 5 to 7.5, heavy phosphate fertilizer, and sandy or eroded soils bring it on.
How to tell it apart

Iron deficiency also yellows young leaves between the veins, but the leaves stay normal in size and do not rosette. Mites and thrips can also stunt new leaves. To be sure, A soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf test. New leaves that come out normal after a zinc spray on a few branches confirm it. In a soil test, less than 0.8 ppm of zinc is low.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Give a foliar spray of 500 grams Zinc sulfate, 250 grams lime and 100 grams urea with 100 ml soap in 100 liters of water (5 grams Zinc sulfate per liter), three times at 20 day intervals, plus 250 grams Zinc sulfate per tree mixed with compost or manure in two equal doses when the tree puts out new growth. Where the soil is short of zinc, give about 20 kg Zinc sulfate per hectare. Do not apply zinc and phosphate fertilizer at the same time. Give the soil dose at planting or when the rains begin, and sprays on young growth.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc), **Liquid Chelate Zinc with Sulfur** by Sagrex (10 percent zinc and 5 percent sulfur) and **Nemes Foliar** by SCL Filipinas (4.8 0 0 with 10 percent zinc, 4.9 percent boron and 4.8 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid heavy phosphate, keep organic matter up, and include zinc in the program on soils that tested low. Test the soil every two or three years.
Magnesium deficiency in jackfruit

Older, lower leaves turn yellow between the side veins on both sides of the midrib while the veins stay green. The yellow starts at the leaf edge and moves in toward the midrib. Later the yellow parts turn reddish with dead patches, and the leaves drop early. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, often after heavy potash fertilizer.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in langka
Acid, sandy and leached soils, and heavy potash fertilizer, which competes with magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency also hits old leaves, but it burns the leaf edge brown instead of yellowing between the veins. Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole old leaf, veins included. To be sure, do a soil test for magnesium, potassium and calcium, and a leaf test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Band about 80 kg Magnesium sulfate per hectare near the trees. Give 1.5 kg Dolomite per tree per year to the soil and a foliar spray of Magnesium sulfate at 10 to 20 grams per liter (160 to 320 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). A 10 to 20 gram per liter spray is strong, so try it on a few branches first. Do not apply magnesium and potassium fertilizers together. Put the soil dose in before planting or when the rains begin. Sprays show results in 10 to 14 days.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use Dolomite when liming acid soils, and keep potash and magnesium in balance based on a soil test.
Iron deficiency in jackfruit

Young leaves yellow between the veins while the veins and midrib stay green. In bad cases the whole young leaf turns yellow, though the midrib can stay green, and growth is stunted. Older leaves usually stay green. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, mostly on high pH soils or after waterlogging.
Why iron deficiency happens in langka

Iron is plentiful in most acid Philippine soils, so true shortage is uncommon. It shows on limestone, coralline or overlimed soils with high pH, and in waterlogged soil. Low potassium can also bring on iron yellowing.
How to tell it apart

Zinc deficiency also yellows young leaves between the veins, but the leaves are small and bunched. Manganese deficiency shows on fully grown leaves as a mix of green and yellow between the main veins. To be sure, A soil test for pH and iron. Many soils here already hold a lot of iron. So use a soil test to find the real cause before adding iron.
What to apply for iron deficiency

Where the soil is short of iron, give about 15 kg Ferrous sulfate per hectare. Use chelated iron (EDDHA) as a soil drench on high pH soils, since iron sprays on the leaves generally work poorly. Ferrous sulfate to the soil on acid soils. Improve drainage where water stands. Spray Ferrous sulfate at 0.5 to 1 percent (80 to 160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer), or an iron chelate at the label rate, two or three times 7 to 10 days apart.

Sold here with iron: **DDDD Planter's Choice Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Modern Time (19 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl Chem (30 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulphate Monohydrate** by Newman Chemicals (30 percent iron) and **Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not overlime, drain wet spots, and keep potash up. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any jackfruit nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your langka needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Jackfruit nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my langka leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: the whole canopy turns pale green, older leaves go yellow and drop, and new shoots stay short. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at boron deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in jackfruit?
items.a: For young trees, the Philippine practice described by Coronel gives 100 to 150 grams of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per tree one month after planting and the same again six months later. Fruiting trees take 0.5 to 1 kg of Complete 14 14 14 each when the rains begin and the same amount again as they end.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in jackfruit?
items.a: Give potash with the yearly fertilizer, following the soil test. Feed each EVIARC Sweet tree 0.83 kg Complete 14 14 14, 3.33 kg Solophos and 0.73 kg Muriate of potash 0 0 60.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in jackfruit?
items.a: Apply a phosphorus fertilizer in a ring under the canopy and work it into the topsoil, following the soil test. Give 3.33 kg Solophos (Superphosphate 0 20 0) per tree, along with complete fertilizer and potash.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my langka lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the jackfruit nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
